summary: GCP service account rotation + least-privilege role grant for infra-team CI runners
description:
Issue summary:
Request to rotate the long-lived GCP service account keys used by the infra-team CI runners and to grant a narrowly scoped set of IAM permissions to the new service account. Goal is to follow least-privilege principles and satisfy upcoming SOC audit questions about key rotation cadence.

Impact:
- CI pipelines in prod-us-east intermittently fail when keys are changed without coordinated rollout.
- If rotation is not performed, audit will flag a finding for >90-day key lifetime.

Environment:
- Projects: redwood-prod, redwood-staging
- CI runners: infra-ci-runner-1 (prod-us-east), infra-ci-runner-2 (staging-eu-west)

Background and rationale:
- Current service account redwood-ci-sa has an old key created 2025-11-01. Security asked for rotation and evidence of least-privilege mapping.
- Previous rotation (INT-4127) covered cross-project role mappings but did not update CI runner keys.

Requested changes:
1) Create a new service account redwood-ci-sa-v2 in redwood-prod and redwood-staging projects.
2) Bind a minimal custom role (custom role: roles/redwood.ciRunner) with the following permissions: 
   - resourcemanager.projects.get
   - storage.objects.get
   - storage.objects.list
   - compute.instances.get (read-only for instance metadata checks)
   - secretmanager.versions.access (only for the specific secret resource)
3) Rotate keys for infra-ci-runner instances by updating the workload identity or replacing long-lived keys depending on infra-team recommendation.
4) Set key expiry and a rotation schedule: 30-day TTL for the key material with documented automation for replacement.

Steps to reproduce / runbook:
- See Confluence runbook linked above. High-level flow: create SA -> create key / configure workload identity -> deploy to CI runner pool -> monitor pipeline success for 24 hours -> revoke old key.

Justification for access:
- The infra team needs read access to project metadata and storage artifacts to run build/test steps. Write permissions are intentionally omitted.

Requestor note: 
- Tightly scoped access required for CI; request temporary elevated permissions for the rotation ops only. Expiry requested: 2026-04-10.
comments: 2026-03-10 10:12 - Jordan Lee: Opening ticket. Attached current key fingerprint and last-used timestamps. Asking for rotation window that won't disrupt scheduled releases.

2026-03-10 13:45 - Maya Patel (IAM): Acknowledged. Can you confirm whether the runners are configured to use workload identity or a JSON key on disk? Workload identity would avoid key rotation complexity.

2026-03-10 15:02 - Jordan Lee: infra-ci-runner-1 still uses a mounted JSON key (legacy). Runner team is open to switching to workload identity but needs a short maintenance window to test. We prefer a staged approach to avoid breaking nightly builds.

2026-03-11 09:20 - Rishi Kumar (Security): Please ensure the custom role excludes any iam.serviceAccounts.actAs permissions. If runners need to impersonate, use a separate short-lived impersonation flow and document it for the audit trail.

2026-03-12 11:34 - Maya Patel (IAM): Created draft custom role JSON in repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/1290. Proposed permissions reviewed by Security. Next step: create SA v2 and test in staging-eu-west.

2026-03-13 08:50 - Priya Shah (CI): Staging test succeeded with new SA and workload identity binding. Production rollout requires a 2-hour maintenance window to swap keys on runner instances. Scheduling with Release Ops.
2026-03-13 16:05 - Maya Patel (IAM): Scoped permission changes applied to staging project. Will schedule prod SA creation and rollout after confirmation from Release Ops. Marking ticket In Progress)
investigation_notes: Checked audit logs for redwood-ci-sa: last key usage pattern shows frequent GETs to storage objects between 02:00-05:00 UTC (nightly test runs). Link: https://console.cloud.google.com/logs/query;query=resource.type%3D%22service_account%22
Validated no existing impersonation workflows depend on iam.serviceAccounts.actAs for redwood-ci-sa in staging (scoped check via gcloud iam roles describe).
Verified CI runner AMIs/containers: runners mount secret at /etc/ci/keys/redwood-ci.json (old pattern). Work planned to move to workload identity provider (WIF) to eliminate long-lived keys.

Risk assessment: If we rotate key without updating runners, pipelines will fail. Plan includes deploying new SA + workload identity in staging, running 48-hour verification, then rotating prod key during maintenance window.
resolution_notes: Staging: new SA created and workload identity bound; pipelines validated for 24h with no failures. Old key removed from staging mounts. (See PR #1290)
Production: awaiting scheduled 2-hour maintenance window from Release Ops. Post-rollout tasks: revoke old key, record rotation in audit log, update runbook with observed rollback steps.

Follow-up: automate rotation using Cloud Scheduler + Cloud Functions to generate and upload short-lived keys OR migrate all runners to Workload Identity within 30 days. Security to re-evaluate after prod rollout.
